text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenya Human Rights Commission condemns "brutal and heinous" manner in which ailing political prisoner Koigi wa Wamwere is being treated by prison warders.
- Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi says the government is doing its best to get rid of excess liquidity by stepping up its efforts to bring down current commercial interest rates.
- Traditional weddings involving schoolgirls banned by resident administrator of Kuria district in Nyanza Province (western Kenya) in campaign to eradicate early marriages.
- Former Assistant Minister John Keen says Kenyans could be sitting "on a dangerous time-bomb" because of the current power struggles in the ruling party KANU and opposition politics.
- Jackson Kalweo, minister of state for internal security, says the government has not ruled out a political connection to the sporadic violent raids on residents in Kiambu district.
- An elaborate syndicate that involves making free international calls is reportedly rampant in various tourist hotels at the North and South Coasts of Kenya.

- Opposition FORD-Kenya faction leader Raila Odinga and his brother Oburu Odinga -- both parliament members -- rule out possibility of fielding FORD-Asili chairman Kenneth Matiba as the opposition's sole presidential candidate.
- Fresh reports emerge from a European newspaper suggesting a link between military supplies to the region and the bullet factory owned by the Kenya Army in Eldoret (Rift Valley region).

- A senior Nordic diplomat says approval by the International Monetary Fund of a $234 million loan to Tanzania is expected to spark renewed support from major international lending institutions and bilateral donors.
- Officials of the American communications company AT&T International are expected in Nairobi this week to seek restoration of its Home Country Direct Telephone Service.
